prompt: You are now from West Virginia. Someone just assumed it was 'part of regular Virginia.' Defend your state with your whole chest.
response:
Well, now hold on just a minute there, friend. I’m gonna pretend I didn’t just hear that, for your sake. But since you brought it up, let’s get a few things straight, and I mean straight as a coal seam.

First off, we ain’t “part of regular Virginia.” We *divorced* Virginia. And we had the best reason in the whole, entire history of this country to do it. Back in 1861, when the rest of Virginia voted to secede from the Union to go fight for the right to keep people in chains, the folks out here in these mountains said, “Absolutely not.” We weren’t plantation country. We were a land of hard-working miners, farmers, and loggers who didn’t own slaves and sure weren’t gonna die for the rich man’s right to. We held our own little meeting in Wheeling, declared the Richmond government void, and formed our own state—the only state in the Union born out of the Civil War. “Montani Semper Liberi,” baby: Mountaineers Are Always Free. We seceded from the secessionists. How’s that for a history lesson?

And don’t you dare think we’re just some leftover chunk of a state. We’re the heart and soul of Appalachia. We’re not a “part” of anything. We’re the Mountain State, and these ancient, rolling mountains don’t just separate us geographically; they’ve forged an entire culture. We’re a people of self-reliance. You think a flatlander from Richmond knows how to fix a truck with baling wire and sheer will? You think they know what a ramp is, or how to make a proper pepperoni roll that’d make a grown man weep? I didn’t think so.

We powered the Industrial Revolution with the coal from our guts. We built the skyscrapers of New York and the battleships that won two world wars, and we did it with broken backs and black lung, for a “thank you” that never came. We gave the world Chuck Yeager, the man who broke the sound barrier—a kid from Hamlin who was too tough for gravity itself. We’ve got Mother’s Day started right here in Grafton. We’ve got the New River, which is actually one of the oldest rivers on the planet, and the New River Gorge Bridge, a steel arch so beautiful and massive they have a whole day, Bridge Day, where people just jump off it with parachutes. You think there’s a “Bridge Day” in Fairfax County? Please.

So, no. We’re not “regular Virginia.” The very idea is an insult. “Regular Virginia” is for people who sip wine and sit in traffic on I-95. West Virginia is for folks who know how to navigate a holler without GPS, who’ll pull your car out of a ditch without asking for a dime, and who still believe a hard day’s work and your word are your bond. We’re wild, we’re wonderful, and we are perfectly, distinctly, and eternally separate. Now, you want to try that statement again, or do you want a hot pepperoni roll to go with that slice of humble pie?
